doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Closing thoughts on talent and goodbyes
summary: Havens says he was lucky and that jazz needs natural talent; thanks and goodbyes.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well this has been fascinating, and thanks so much for sharing your time with us.

Well it’s been a pleasure talking with you, Monk. I hope this is beneficial to whoever likes to observe it. I always like to talk about my career, because I feel really fortunate that things just sort of fell into place. I never really had to work at progressing in my career. I seemed to be at the right place at the right time, which is very fortunate. But you know I think when it comes to jazz, you have to have some natural talent to really go far with it. It’s something that schooling doesn’t do a complete job with. You have to have that inside of you, you’re like sort of born with it.
I agree. All right well on behalf of Hamilton College, thank you very much, and good luck in Branson and tonight, with your music.
Thank you, Monk. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
